rationale: Block 3 establishes the four Plasmodium species with distinguishing features; Dialogcards test recall of each species' key characteristics as related prompt→answer pairs.
Block 4 explains the malaria fever mechanism via haemozoin and the cytokine cascade; this question tests understanding of the pathogenesis that drives the classic paroxysm.

Block 5 clarifies the G6PD–primaquine interaction; this statement tests whether students correctly understand that chloroquine remains safe in G6PD deficiency — only the radical cure needs modification.

Block 6 details peripheral smear features distinguishing all four species; this spatial-identification task tests the most examined practical skill — matching species to their characteristic smear appearance.

rationale: Block 8 covers the full malaria diagnostic algorithm; this question tests understanding that a single negative smear does not exclude malaria and that repeat testing is standard practice.
Block 9 covers kala-azar and filariasis; this question tests application of diagnostic knowledge for visceral leishmaniasis in an Indian field setting where microscopy may be unavailable.

Block 3 describes HIV structure including the error-prone reverse transcriptase; this question tests understanding of why RT's high error rate is the molecular basis for drug resistance and combination therapy.
Block 5 describes the stepwise HIV entry and replication mechanism; ordering these steps tests recall of the pathogenesis sequence from receptor binding to latent reservoir formation.
Block 7 establishes CD4-based OI thresholds; this question tests application of the threshold concept to a clinical presentation consistent with the AIDS-defining CD4 <200 level.
Block 8 explains IRIS; this statement tests whether students can distinguish paradoxical IRIS worsening from ART treatment failure — a critical clinical misconception.
Block 9 covers HIV diagnostic methods including EID by PCR; this question tests application of the principle that transplacental maternal antibodies invalidate ELISA in infants under 18 months.
Block 11 covers prevention strategies including PEP and PrEP; this question tests the critical time window for initiating post-exposure prophylaxis after occupational exposure.
